Can a login be attempted right now

Source: R/protection.R
aa_login_gate.Rd

A single check before verifying the password: first the global failure limit across all logins, then the lockout of this login. If login is closed, there is no need to verify the password, and no need to record the attempt (otherwise the lockout would be extended).

Usage

aa_login_gate(conn, login, settings = aa_settings())

Arguments

conn

A connection to the SQLite database (DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ...)).

login

The entered login (exact, case-sensitive).

settings

Settings, the result of aa_settings().

Value

A list: allowed (TRUE or FALSE), reason (NA, "throttled" for the global limit or "locked" for a login lockout), seconds (how many seconds are left until the login lockout ends, otherwise 0) and message (text to show to the user in the settings language, NA if login is allowed).

Details

The function does not stop login on an error: if the protection tables do not exist or cannot be queried, login is considered allowed (the password is still verified) and the reason is written to the app log. This way an unavailable attempts table does not lock out all users.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("RSQLite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
  aa_init_db(conn)
  aa_login_gate(conn, "alsey")$allowed
  for (i in 1:5) aa_record_attempt(conn, "alsey", FALSE)
  aa_login_gate(conn, "alsey")
  DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
}
